name: IIFL Finance Ltd
tagline: A diversified retail NBFC that has fully recovered from the 2024 RBI gold-loan ban - FY26 PAT +183%, ROE back near 20%, AUM ~Rs 1.08 lakh Cr - but a ~Rs 25,700 Cr large-cap with a chequered governance history and no 10x math. Snippet-tracked by @a_basumallick, not a call.
business_overview: Retail-focused NBFC: gold loans (~Rs 57-58k Cr AUM, the growth engine), home finance + LAP (~Rs 40k Cr), microfinance and digital loans. Uses a large co-lending / assignment (off-book) model. Recovered from a six-month RBI ban on new gold-loan disbursement (Mar-Sep 2024). Seeded as a trusted-X WATCH item: @a_basumallick relayed a CNBC-TV18 snippet that Blackstone may buy up to 20% of IIFL Finance with Fairfax exiting - neutral PE-activity framing, explicitly NOT a conviction call.

Rs 586 Cr (+~183% YoY); Q4FY26 PAT Rs 586 Cr line reflects strong H2
GNPA ~2.6% blended; MFI segment carrying elevated provisions
~Rs 475 Cr income-tax demand (under appeal); legacy NSEL / IIFL Commodities property-attachment matter
fundamentals_narrative: Operationally IIFL Finance is back on track: the gold-loan book has been rebuilt (+~150% YoY), consolidated AUM is ~Rs 1.08 lakh Cr (+38%), FY26 PAT is up ~183% and ROE is back near 20%. Off-book / assignment income is a large and growing share of revenue. The negatives are structural rather than cyclical: it is a ~Rs 25,700 Cr large-cap (no 10x path), it carries a governance track record (the RBI ban itself, the historic NSEL / IIFL Commodities matter, LODR-era issues across the group) and MFI-segment stress keeps provisions elevated. Valuation at ~1.8x book / ~13x earnings with the stock near its high already reflects the recovery.

verdict_headline: Operationally recovered, ROE near 20%, but a large-cap NBFC with a governance history and no 10x math - and the trusted-X item is an explicit non-call. thesis_fit 'neither', conviction Medium. Tier-4.8 watch: exits with a last_analyzed_date.
verdict_reasoning: four_box: tailwind weak (gold-price + financialisation tailwind, but the post-ban rebound is normalisation not a new structural driver), tam yes (retail-credit TAM is large), moat weak (diversified retail NBFC with distribution scale but no strong moat; governance history a negative), valuation weak (~1.8x book / ~13x earnings, recovery largely priced, near highs) -> score 2.5

Genuine large-cap (~Rs 25,700 Cr) -> tam effectively 'no' for the required multiple -> thesis_fit 'neither' on size math. The large-cap named-inflection exception does NOT apply: a private-equity stake purchase is ownership churn, not the management / regulatory / capital-allocation turnaround the exception contemplates.
Conviction Medium: quality has genuinely recovered (ROE ~20%, AUM +38%, PAT +183%) which keeps it off Low-Medium, but the governance track record and absence of thesis fit cap it at Medium

No red-flag tier (disclosed, worked-through legacy matters; no active fraud order)

four_box.note: Genuine large-cap -> tam cannot deliver the required multiple (treat as 'no' for the thesis); label 'neither' on size math. tailwind weak (post-ban normalisation, not a new structural driver), moat weak (retail NBFC, governance history), valuation weak (~1.8x book, recovery priced). Large-cap inflection exception not applicable (PE stake = ownership churn).

quality_metrics.note: NBFC lending business - net_debt_to_ebitda/interest_coverage/fcf_conversion_pct are not meaningful metrics for this business model (leverage is structural to lending) and are left null rather than guessed. roce_pct/roce_trend use ROE as the closest analog: 18% (FY24) -> 5% (FY25, the RBI gold-loan-ban year) -> 13% (FY26) -> ~19.5% (Q1 FY27) - a genuine, ongoing recovery, not yet back to pre-ban levels. NIM stable/mildly compressing (7.0% Mar-25 -> 6.8% Jun-25).

track_record.note: Uses total revenue/income (in place of 'revenue growth', not meaningful in the same sense for an NBFC) and ROE (in place of ROCE). FY22 (+17.1% revenue, ROE 20%), FY23 (+20.8%, ROE 19%) and FY24 (+24.0%, ROE 18%) each cleared BOTH >=10% growth and >=15% ROE; FY25 broke the streak on revenue (-2.3%, the RBI gold-loan-ban year) and FY26 on ROE (13%, still recovering) despite revenue growth resuming (+30.6%) - a clean, honest record of a real disruption and an ongoing, not-yet-complete recovery.
